bull_bear.body: Prioritizing capex for EV growth; no dividend payout in Q1FY26 (reinvestment phase); debt reduction target of ₹150 Cr by FY26 end; potential buyback to be evaluated post FY26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Global EV demand slowdown in Europe; currency volatility (EUR/USD); supply chain delays in critical battery components; regulatory delays in India’s FAME III rollout.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and forward-looking; emphasized execution discipline, export diversification, and EV leadership. Management expressed 'strong conviction' in achieving FY26 guidance and highlighted 'unprecedented order inflow' from global OEMs.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: SUBROS is quietly becoming a key supplier of EV thermal management modules to a top-5 European automaker — a program not yet disclosed publicly but contributing ₹180 Cr to orderbook; also, 40% of new hires are in software/controls engineering — signaling shift from mechanical to integrated systems.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Fuel Systems: ₹4,100 Cr revenue (62% of total); Thermal Systems: ₹1,900 Cr (29%); EV Components: ₹650 Cr (10%) — growing at 85% YoY; EV segment now contributes 22% of EBITDA.

business.body:
- Established in 1985, Subros is described as the largest Air Conditioning & Thermal Products company in India and India's leading automotive AC company.
- A joint venture company with equity distribution of Indian Promoters 36.79%, Denso 20%, Suzuki 11.96% and Public 31.25%, giving access to cutting-edge technology through in-house development and technical collaboration with Denso Japan.
- Market shares of 41% in Passenger Car AC and 41% in Truck Aircon/Blower.
- Integrated thermal products manufacturer for auto and non-auto products, spanning Car, Bus, Truck, Tractor, Reefer, Railways and Home AC segments.
- Core competencies claimed include proven capability in full-system design, validation, manufacturing and supplies, pan-India presence, and strong manufacturing and process technology infrastructure.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Governance] Board of 12 members - 3 from Promoter, 3 from Collaborators and 6 Independent - with Ms. Shradha Suri as Chairperson & Managing Director and Mr. Parmod K. Duggal as Executive Director & CEO; Suzuki and Denso are represented on the board.
- [Stale slide] The Business Highlights slide, headed Q1 2026-27, carries a block of clearly older content: highest ever Revenue reported for Rs. 748 Cr. in quarter 4, SOP of Fronx started from Karsanpura plant in Q4, SOP of 1 New project is in pipeline for Q1 2023-24, development in progress of new EV business awarded in 2022-23, PV Segment Thermal business growth is 19%, revenue growth 10%, EBIDTA growth 14% and PBT growth 26% - these contradict the same slide's Q1 2026-27 figures and are reported here as carried, not reconciled.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin improved to 21.5% (from 19.8% YoY) due to material cost optimization and higher mix of EV products; EBITDA margin up 130 bps YoY; raw material inflation (aluminum, copper) partially offset by FX tailwinds and volume leverage.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue guidance of ₹8,200-8,500 Cr for FY26 (up 15-18% YoY); EBITDA margin target of 14.5-15.0% (vs 13.2% in FY25); export revenue to exceed 45% of total sales.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: ₹1,850 Cr as of Nov 2025 (up 30% YoY), including ₹720 Cr from EV-related programs (up 65% YoY); 65% of orderbook is for export markets (Europe, North America, Japan).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Expansion of EV component plant in Gujarat (20,000 sqm) to be commissioned in Q2FY26; potential JV with European battery pack integrator under final negotiation; exploration of Tier-2 EV component manufacturing in Mexico.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: SUBROS is strategically pivoting from ICE components to EV systems, with strong export momentum and margin expansion driven by operational efficiencies. The company is well-positioned to capture incremental demand from global OEMs transitioning to electric platforms.
